Lumen Rail

Desk sample · Field Desk

The concession

Lumen Rail is not a transit agency you can ride. It is the sample franchise in this repository: a city-owned concession that runs a light line along a river the demo never names on a map you could navigate.

The night timetable is a public document. In the story, it is posted at every platform and filed at the yard office. In the CMS, it is a paragraph an editor can move.

The sheet. Structured facts stay in fields so a writer is not asked to invent a layout.

What the concession records

  1. Story year1978
  2. Gauge1,435 mm
  3. Stations24
  4. Night span18 minutes
  5. Owner in the storyThe city

The office that holds the concession is a room above the carbarn. The sample describes it with a window toward the river and a cabinet of paper timetables. None of those details are drawn from a published Artometrics story. They exist so the template has something true to its own fiction.

Note

Sample concession, clause 4

If the sheet is public, the yard does not get to be a rumor.

How the yard runs

1. Cars come off the river span and wait under the shed.
2. The night sheet is copied before the last southbound leaves.
3. A fault on the span holds the following car at the previous station.
4. The cabinet copy and the platform copy are meant to match.

A writer using this template can lift the list above the heading, or drop the figure under the quote. The order in the file is the order on the page. Publishing copies that order into the static build. Saving does not.

What riders meet

Platforms in the story are concrete, lit, and short on ornament. Riders meet a clock, a posted sheet, and the river at their back. The demo stops there. It does not invent a fare table or a real city charter.
